ta-gu-waterfall: Tà Gụ Waterfall in Nha Trang. Commit to Khánh Sơn / Sơn Hiệp country for Tà Gụ, a ~40 m cascade sourced near 1,300 m on Hòn Bà. White water on grey rock in primary forest — a long road day, not a Nha Trang afternoon. A 40-metre forest fall off Hòn Bà, far west of the city.
suoi-thach-lam: Ticketed eco park, not a wilderness reserve. Do not confuse it with Suối Mơ (a different eco zone) or Suối Tiên.
hon-ba-nature-reserve: Protected forest southwest of Nha Trang. Access, gates, and research-station rules change — go with a licensed driver or tour.
nha-trang-beach: Nha Trang Beach (Trần Phú Beach) in Nha Trang. Swim the municipal beach that made Nha Trang a resort city: pale sand, morning locals, loungers, and a steepish shore break in front of the hotel wall. The promenade card is the walkway; this card is the water. The city’s 6 km crescent of sand in front of Trần Phú.
bai-duong-beach: Free public/resort-adjacent beach on the north shore. Not Dốc Lết (that is Ninh Hòa) and not Bãi Dài (Cam Ranh).
doc-let-beach: Some resort gates charge ~50,000 VND. Combine with Điệp Sơn if you already have a tour van; do not hire two cars.
bai-dai-beach: Bãi Dài (Long Beach, Cam Ranh) in Nha Trang. Ride south toward the airport peninsula for Bãi Dài — kilometres of open sand and resort gardens, quieter and windier than Trần Phú, used as a beach day when you have a Cam Ranh arrival or an extra night. The long resort beach on the Cam Ranh peninsula.
hon-tre-island: Reached by cable car from the south mainland station (about 8 minutes) or boat in bad weather. Park tickets often include the gondola.
hon-tam-island: Hòn Tằm Island (Silkworm Island) in Nha Trang. Boat to Hòn Tằm for a managed beach day: sand, lunch decks, and optional spa, sold as a quieter alternative to VinWonders. The island name means silkworm; the product is a ticketed shore, not a village. A resort-and-beach islet 7 km off the city.
hon-mun-island: 15–20 minutes by speedboat from Cầu Đá, or 60–90 on a wooden day boat. A small marine-park fee is often bundled.
hon-mieu-island: Hòn Miếu Island in Nha Trang. Land on Hòn Miếu, the inshore island south of Cầu Đá, for Bãi Tranh swimming and the Trí Nguyên ship aquarium. Most four-island boats call here first because the crossing is short. The nearest inhabited island: aquarium ship and Bãi Tranh.
hon-mot-island: Almost always a stop on a multi-island boat, not a solo ferry. If your ticket already lists Hòn Mun + Hòn Một, do not add this as a second day.
hon-lao-island: North of the city in Nha Phu Bay, often paired with Hoa Lan. Adult tickets often ~126,000 VND plus boat.
hoa-lan-island: Đảo Hoa Lan (Orchid Island) in Nha Trang. Visit Hoa Lan (Orchid Island / Suối Hoa Lan on some tickets) in the lagoon north of Nha Trang: a managed beach-and-garden island often combined with Hòn Lao, not the city-bay four-island loop. A ticketed eco-islet in Nha Phu Bay.
diep-son-island: Điệp Sơn Island (Sandbar Island) in Nha Trang. Wade the famous shallow sandbar linking Điệp Sơn’s islets (Hòn Bịp, Hòn Giữa, Hòn Đuốc) in Vạn Ninh, about 60 km north. The path sits in ankle-to-knee water at typical tides — the photograph everyone comes for. A 700-metre sand path that walks you into Vân Phong Bay.
ninh-van-bay: Resorts are boat-access and priced accordingly. Independent travelers can still stop at roadside viewpoints on the way to Ba Hồ.
van-phong-bay: A region, not a single ticket booth. Most visitors see it via Điệp Sơn / Dốc Lết / Đầm Môn tours.
vinwonders-nha-trang: VinWonders Nha Trang (Vinpearl Land) in Nha Trang. Spend a full ticketed day on Hòn Tre at VinWonders (formerly Vinpearl Land, opened 2006): rides, Tropical Paradise water park, Sea World tunnel, King’s Garden, and night shows. Round-trip cable car is usually included. Vietnam’s largest island theme park at the cable-car landing.
vinpearl-harbor: Vinpearl Harbor in Nha Trang. Walk the purpose-built harbour district on Hòn Tre: dining streets, a night-market food row, go-karts and add-on shows. It sits beside VinWonders but is sold as its own cable + district ticket when you do not want the full park. Harbour town, night market, and shows on Hòn Tre.
thap-ba-hot-springs: Tháp Bà Hot Springs & Mud Bath in Nha Trang. Soak in the Tháp Bà (Lady Tower) springs northwest of the Cham towers: sodium-silicate water from about 38–72 °C, communal or private mud tubs, then mineral pools. One of Vietnam’s first commercial hot-spring parks. The original 1994 mineral-mud complex behind Po Nagar.
i-resort-mud-bath: I-Resort Mud Bath in Nha Trang. Spend a half-day at I-Resort’s outdoor mud tubs under trees, mineral waterfalls, and swimming pools on the north-west edge of town — a more landscaped, family-scale alternative to Tháp Bà’s older site. The larger mineral campus in Vĩnh Ngọc: mud, falls, and pools.
hundred-egg-mud-bath: 100 Egg Mud Bath (Khu Du Lịch Trăm Trứng) in Nha Trang. Sit in the trademark oval “egg” tubs at Trăm Trứng in Phước Đồng — a cheaper, photogenic mud park on the south highway, with mineral soak and simple grounds rather than I-Resort’s scale. Egg-shaped mud pods on Nguyễn Tất Thành.
suoi-mo: Suối Mơ Eco Tourism Zone in Nha Trang. Spend a low-key family day at Suối Mơ — Dream Stream — an eco-tourism zone of shallow water, picnic lawns, and simple play, used by Nha Trang residents more than island-boat tourists. A local stream-and-garden park west of the city.
nha-trang-promenade: Trần Phú Boulevard Promenade in Nha Trang. Walk Trần Phú’s paved promenade along the crescent: sunrise exercisers, hotel terraces, Trầm Hương Tower at 2/4 Square, and evening lights. This is the boulevard, not the swimming-beach card. The long seaside walk from morning swimmers to neon.
dam-market: Đầm Market (Chợ Đầm) in Nha Trang. Move through Chợ Đầm, Nha Trang’s main multi-storey market: produce, dry goods, cheap clothes, and a food wing that still feeds locals. It is a working hall, not a designed night bazaar. The city’s big covered market behind the station quarter.
xom-moi-market: Xóm Mới Market in Nha Trang. Eat at Chợ Xóm Mới, the local market west of the tourist beach where residents shop fish, herbs, and morning soup. Bún cá and bánh canh stalls here are the practical order, not lacquer boxes. The neighborhood wet market for bún cá and breakfast.
nha-trang-night-market: Nha Trang Night Market in Nha Trang. Wander the night market that sets up along Trần Phú and the streets behind the hotel wall: grilled seafood, cheap clothes, and souvenirs aimed at walkers coming off the promenade. It is seasonal in density, not a historic covered hall. Evening stalls along the beach boulevard.
skylight-nha-trang: Skylight Nha Trang (360° Skydeck, Havana Hotel) in Nha Trang. Ride to the Havana Hotel skydeck — Skylight’s glass-walled bar and outdoor platforms — for a paid sunset circuit of the bay, Hòn Tre, and the Trần Phú grid. The product is the view and a drink minimum, not a museum. A rooftop 360° deck over the crescent beach.
cai-rang-floating-market: Cái Răng Floating Market is the largest wholesale floating market in the Mekong Delta, situated on the Hậu River in Cần Thơ. Visitors ride out at dawn to see produce boats displaying their goods on long bamboo poles amid a maze of river traffic.
phong-dien-floating-market: Experience the quieter canal market, operating earlier and more locally than Cai Rang down narrow waterways. Watch long-tail boats trade bulk produce directly between boat dwellers.
ninh-kieu-wharf: Ninh Kieu Wharf serves as Can Tho's primary river hub where morning longtail boats depart for the Cai Rang floating market and evening lights illuminate the Hau River. It functions as a dynamic working pier and public park rather than a static historical monument.
moi-canal: Drift or cycle Rach Moi, one of the city's named canals featuring stilt houses, orchards, and small boats. It offers river texture without another early morning tourist alarm.
chua-ong-can-tho: Ông Temple (Chùa Ông – Quảng Đông Assembly Hall) in Can Tho, Mekong. Step into the 1894–96 Quảng Đông (Quảng Triệu) assembly hall at about 32 Hai Bà Trưng: carved wood, red lanterns, and a sanctuary to Quan Công used by Cần Thơ’s Hoa community. It is a hội quán, not a Khmer wat. Cantonese incense and Quan Công on Hai Bà Trưng.
nam-nha-pagoda: Nam Nha Pagoda is an 1895 river pagoda in Can Tho that served as a Minh Su hall and a historic liaison point for anti-colonial organisers. Visitors can explore its yellow Franco-Asian halls and pair the stop with the nearby Binh Thuy Ancient House.
phuoc-hau-pagoda: Pay respects at Chua Phuoc Hau, a local Bac tong monastery in greater Can Tho. Experience incense halls and a courtyard used by neighbourhood Buddhists rather than dawn-market groups.
pothi-somron: Pôthi SômRôn is a tranquil Theravāda Khmer monastery in the Ô Môn district of Can Tho. It offers visitors a rural village wat rhythm featuring pointed roofs and colored prang details, distinct from urban pagodas.
munir-ansay: Chùa Munir Ansay is Can Tho's prominent Khmer Theravada pagoda located right on Dai lo Hoa Binh. It serves as an active community center and monastic residence featuring distinct regional architecture.
quang-duc-pagoda: Free, ~2 km from Ninh Kiều. Do not confuse with the self-immolation monk Thích Quảng Đức’s memorials in Saigon — this is a different dedication.
truc-lam-phuong-nam: Spend a quieter hour at Trúc Lâm Phương Nam on TL 923 in Mỹ Khánh, Phong Điền: a southern branch of the Trúc Lâm zen lineage with broad courtyards and lotus ponds. This large campus offers a monastery scale that city wats cannot match.
can-tho-cathedral: Can Tho Cathedral is the mother parish of the local diocese, offering a peaceful, working worship space on Hoà Bình Avenue. It stands as a modest colonial-era ecclesiastical landmark distinct from the city's busier shrines.
binh-thuy-ancient-house: Bình Thủy Ancient House in Can Tho, Mekong. Tour Nhà cổ Bình Thủy on Bùi Hữu Nghĩa: a ~150-year mix of French colonial and Nam Bộ woodwork, high ceilings, and a courtyard still associated with the Dương lineage and period films including The Lover. An 1870s Dương-family timber house used as a film set.
can-tho-grand-prison: Walk through the 1886 French provincial prison, now a preserved national relic in central Can Tho. Explore the cell blocks, watch posts, and regional exhibits documenting the hard history of political imprisonment in the western Mekong Delta.
can-tho-museum: The largest provincial museum campus in the delta, located on Hoà Bình. It provides essential context for the river you just rode at dawn.
military-zone-9-museum: The Military Zone 9 Museum in Can Tho offers a focused look at the regional history of the Mekong Delta's armed conflicts. It serves as a significant repository for documents and heavy military hardware used during decades of intense warfare.
hcm-museum-can-tho: Hồ Chí Minh Museum (Cần Thơ Branch) in Can Tho, Mekong. See the Cần Thơ branch of the Hồ Chí Minh Museum — rooms on his life and the delta’s relationship with him, including the “Studying Uncle Hồ” civic display — inside 6 Hoà Bình, not a separate river site. The 1990 HCM galleries inside the Military Zone 9 campus.
bang-lang-stork: Bằng Lăng Stork Sanctuary is a private, decades-old haven for thousands of waterbirds in the Mekong Delta. It offers a rare, immersive experience of observing diverse avian species returning to their bamboo canopy at dusk.
con-son: Cồn Sơn is a community-run islet in the Hậu River where residents host visitors in their own orchards and homes. It offers an intimate look at Mekong Delta life through fruit tasting, traditional cake making, and the famous flying snakehead fish demonstration.
con-au: Cross to Cồn Ấu for a slower river-island walk: local gardens and views back to the city shore without Cồn Sơn’s fish-show circuit. An islet if you already did the community-tourism script.
con-khuong: Con Khuong is a quiet, residential river islet in the Hau River, offering an authentic look at Mekong Delta life away from the crowds. It is best visited as a peaceful, unhurried stop during a broader boat tour of the local river landscape.
my-khanh-village: A 20-hectare delta in miniature located in Phong Dien district. It offers a ticketed afternoon of orchards, folk games, animals, and snack stalls for families.
giot-dang-orchard: Sit down at Giọt Đắng or Chín Hồng, two well-known Phong Điền canal-side orchards functioning as garden restaurants. Experience a real orchard lunch and fresh fruit tasting rather than a ticketed tourist path.
ba-lang-gardens: Stop in Ba Láng for smallholder fruit gardens that boatmen add after the floating market: longan, mango, and seasonal tasting tables on the same water as the wholesale. This is the orchard that does not need a Phong Điền transfer.
lung-ngoc-hoang: Lung Ngọc Hoàng Nature Reserve is a sprawling 2,800-hectare wetland sanctuary in the Mekong Delta, serving as a vital ecological lung for the region. It offers a rare, immersive experience into the wild tràm forest ecosystem, providing a quiet refuge for birdlife and a glimpse into the delta's original, untamed landscape.
ninh-kieu-love-bridge: Walk Cầu đi bộ Ninh Kiều — Cầu Tình Yêu — about 200 m of LED-lit S-curve over Rạch Khai Luông, opened February 2016, linking the wharf park to Cái Khế’s play shore. The city’s evening photograph, not a second river tour.
can-tho-bridge: Cần Thơ Bridge is a massive 2010 cable-stayed highway span dominating the Hậu River skyline. View it strictly as a civic landmark from riverbanks or boat tours since pedestrian access is prohibited.
can-tho-old-market: Walk the historic riverside market hall on Hai Bà Trưng street to experience Cần Thơ daily trade. The tiled hall and surrounding stalls feed the city by morning, just minutes away from Chùa Ông.
can-tho-night-market: Eat through the night stalls that fill Hai Ba Trung and the wharf edge after dusk: grilled skewers, fruit, and cheap clothes. Locals also call this stretch Cho dem Ninh Kieu.
tay-do-market: Tay Do Market serves as the vibrant evening identity of Can Tho's renovated riverside marketplace along the Hau River. It combines bustling retail stalls, local fruit vendors, and food alleys that blend seamlessly with the adjacent night market.
luu-huu-phuoc-park: Lưu Hữu Phước Park is Can Tho's central green space named after the celebrated musician. It offers shaded walkways, fitness areas, and a local atmosphere away from the tourist wharves.
song-hau-park: Sit in Cong vien Song Hau along the city bank to enjoy river breezes, bridge views, and the local evening crowd. It provides the park layer of the Can Tho waterfront without requiring a separate journey.
ma-pi-leng-pass: Ma Pi Leng Pass in Ha Giang. Ride Đèo Mã Pì Lèng between Đồng Văn and Mèo Vạc — the dramatic shelf of Hạnh Phúc Road, built by volunteer labour through the karst. Designated pull-offs look into Tu Sản canyon; the optional Sky Walk is a separate exposed path. The Happiness Road cut above the Nho Que gorge.
dong-van-geopark: Overnight stays in the four districts may be charged a geopark visitor fee (listings ~30,000 VND/adult/night). The dong-van city card is the same plateau overnight.
quan-ba-heaven-gate: Quan Ba Heaven Gate in Ha Giang. Stop at Cổng Trời Quản Bạ on QL4C, about 40–50 km from the provincial capital: the classic first-day viewpoint over the Twin Mountains valley and the climb onto the plateau. The first high saddle after Hà Giang city — cloud sea if you are lucky.
tu-san-canyon: Viewpoint is a pass stop; the boat is a separate ticket down a steep access. Do not pay twice for “canyon + river” as two full days.
nho-que-river: Nho Que River in Ha Giang. Boat the Nho Que (usually from the Mậu Duệ / Tu Sản access): a dam-raised stretch of jade water through the canyon. Life jackets matter; the climb back to the road is steep. Turquoise reservoir water under Ma Pi Leng’s walls.
tham-ma-pass: Tham Ma Pass in Ha Giang. Ride the tight bends of Thẩm Mã between Yên Minh and Đồng Văn. Local legend names the pass for horses that lost their footing; today it is a short, photogenic shelf with a small shrine stop. Đèo Thẩm Mã — the “horse-trampling” saddle toward Đồng Văn.
chin-khoanh-pass: Chin Khoanh Pass in Ha Giang. Count the bends of Đèo Chín Khoanh — the “nine-section” pass on the Quản Bạ side of the plateau road, a technical stretch more than a viewpoint plaza. Nine hairpins on the climb through Quản Bạ.
bac-sum-pass: Bac Sum Pass in Ha Giang. Cross Đèo Bắc Sum on the first hours of the loop: pine, cloud, and the sense that the plateau has started before Heaven Gate’s official postcard. The early QL4C climb out of Hà Giang city.
quan-ba-twin-mountains: Quan Ba Twin Mountains (Fairy Bosom) in Ha Giang. Photograph the Twin Mountains from Heaven Gate or the valley floor: a pair of limestone hills that local storytelling reads as a fairy’s bosom. Best after rain or in rice green; winter can be grey. Núi Đôi Cô Tiên — two karst breasts in the Quản Bạ valley.
yen-minh-pine-forest: Yen Minh Pine Forest in Ha Giang. Walk or ride through the thông Yên Minh grove used as a loop tea-and-photo stop: cooler air, needle floor, and a pause between Quản Bạ and Thẩm Mã. A roadside pine stand on the way through Yên Minh.
du-gia-waterfall: Pair with Du Già village — one valley, two cards. Off the classic 3-day timing; do not force it after a late Ma Pi Leng.
hoang-su-phi-terraces: Different road from the karst loop. Pair with Chiêu Lầu Thi or Tây Côn Lĩnh, not with Ma Pi Leng the same day.
chieu-lau-thi: Tây Côn Lĩnh (~2,418 m) is the higher Ha Giang massif — do not hike both in 24 hours. Not on the Đồng Văn geopark road.
tay-con-linh: Tay Con Linh Mountain in Ha Giang. Commit to Tây Côn Lĩnh on the Hoàng Su Phì / Vị Xuyên divide: moss forest, waterfalls on the approach, and a long ridge. Higher and wilder than Chiêu Lầu Thi’s cloud meadow reputation. Ha Giang’s highest massif, about 2,418 m on the Chảy headwaters.
lung-khuy-cave: Lung Khuy Cave in Ha Giang. Walk the boarded galleries of Hang Lùng Khúy: a developed karst cave near the Twin Mountains road, with lighting and a modest climb from the ticket booth. A lit limestone cave under Quản Bạ’s hills.
lung-cu-flag-tower: Lung Cu Flag Tower in Ha Giang. Climb Cột cờ Lũng Cú at about 1,470 m: an octagonal tower modelled on Hà Nội’s flag tower, a 54 m² flag for 54 ethnic groups, bronze-drum reliefs, and two ponds locals call a dragon’s eyes. Clear days look into Yunnan. Vietnam’s northern flag, 34.85 m above Lũng Cú commune.
dong-van-ancient-town: Dong Van Ancient Town in Ha Giang. Walk Phố cổ Đồng Văn: late-Nguyễn and French-period façades, a compact square, cafés, and lantern evenings. Restoration is real — it is pleasant, not an untouched trading town. Stone-and-timber shop houses around the highland square.
vuong-palace: Palace of the Hmong King (Vuong Family Palace) in Ha Giang. Tour Dinh Vua Mèo at Sà Phìn: an early-20th-century stone-and-timber compound of the Vương family, blending Chinese courtyard planning with highland Hmong power. The Sà Phìn mansion of Vương Chính Đức / Vương Chí Sình.
meo-vac-town: The market card is the weekly stall morning. Khau Vai is a further commune, not the town square.
yen-minh-town: Pair with the pine forest and Thẩm Mã, then keep moving. Market days are local; do not expect Đồng Văn Sunday density every morning.
ha-giang-km0: Sleep here the night before a 3–4 day loop. The ha-giang-loop card is the road day that starts from this town.
sung-la-valley: Pao’s House and Lao Xa are the same hamlet cluster — one stop. Not a second Sapa terrace.
pao-house: Same stop as Sủng Là / Lao Xa — do not book three village products. Buy hemp only if you want it.
lao-xa-village: Lao Xa Village in Ha Giang. Walk Lao Sa / Lao Xa as a living hamlet: stone fences, hemp, corn cribs. Tourism is concentrated at the film house; the rest is still a village. The Hmong hamlet that holds Pao’s House.
lung-tam-weaving: Free to walk; pay for cloth or a short try-on. Nam Dam is a different (Dao) village nearby — one craft stop is enough unless you care.
du-gia-village: Du Gia Village in Ha Giang. Stay in Du Già: stilt houses, river, and a slower night used on 4-day loops returning to Hà Giang. The waterfall is a walk away; the village is the meal and sleep. A Tày homestay valley and the waterfall’s village.
nam-dam-village: Nam Dam Village in Ha Giang. Visit Nam Dam: Dao houses, community homestays, and a quieter alternative to the Heaven Gate parking lot. Distinct from Lùng Tám’s Hmong looms. A Dao community-tourism village under Quản Bạ.
lo-lo-chai-village: Lo Lo Chai Village in Ha Giang. Walk Lô Lô Chải beside the flag tower: distinctive Lô Lô dress and houses. It is a living border hamlet, easy to turn into a costume stop — don’t. The Lô Lô hamlet under the Lũng Cú flag.
seo-lung-village: Seo Lung Village in Ha Giang. Pass Sẻo Lủng when a driver offers a village that is not on every blog list: stone, corn, and ordinary highland life near the Đồng Văn–Mèo Vạc hills. A quieter Hmong hamlet used as a loop side-stop.
ma-le-village: Same northern spur as the flag. Do not do Lô Lô Chải, Mã Lé, and Lũng Pù in one morning.
lung-pu-village: Lung Pu Village in Ha Giang. Stop at Lũng Pù when the road offers a hamlet above the Nho Que country: ordinary Hmong life, not the flag tower (that is Lũng Cú). A Hmong village on the Mèo Vạc / gorge side of the plateau.
khau-vai-love-market: Khau Vai Love Market site in Ha Giang. Reach Khau Vai commune (Mèo Vạc): historically a gathering where people who could not marry freely met once a year. The lunar festival still happens; the site is marketed year-round and is quieter on ordinary days. The highland meeting ground of the 27th of the 3rd lunar month.
dong-van-sunday-market: Ask before portraits; do not block sales. Mèo Vạc and Quản Bạ have their own weekly days — you cannot honestly do three Sunday markets.
meo-vac-market: Not Khau Vai’s love-market festival. If Sunday is Đồng Văn’s big day, do not expect the same density here the same morning.
quan-ba-market: Quan Ba Market in Ha Giang. Time a Quản Bạ morning market if your calendar hits the local weekly day: Dao, Hmong, and Tày trade closer to Heaven Gate than to Đồng Văn. The first-district market on the climb from the city.
hoang-su-phi-market: Hoang Su Phi Market in Ha Giang. Use Hoàng Su Phì’s market morning when you are already on the terrace side: a different ethnic mix from the Đồng Văn karst Sundays. The west-district highland market — Nùng, Dao, Tày trade.
cat-ba-national-park: Cát Bà National Park preserves a vast expanse of limestone karst forest and marine ecosystems on Vietnam's largest island in the Ha Long Bay archipelago. It serves as the primary habitat for the critically endangered Cát Bà langur and offers diverse trekking routes through dense tropical vegetation.
lan-ha-bay: Lan Ha Bay offers a serene, intimate alternative to the busier waters of Ha Long, featuring hundreds of limestone karsts and quiet, floating fishing villages. Accessible via boat from Cat Ba Island, this protected marine area invites visitors to explore hidden caves, pristine pocket beaches, and a unique, slow-paced maritime ecosystem.
trung-trang-cave: Hang Trung Trang is a developed limestone cave on the Cat Ba national park approach with boardwalks and lights. It provides an accessible first karst experience with about 300 meters of passage.
hospital-cave-cat-ba: Hospital Cave (Hang Quân Y) in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Tour Hang Quân Y (Hospital Cave): 17 rooms on three levels, used as a secret hospital and command post during the American War. Concrete floors, hospital fittings, and a short film or guide at busy times. A bombproof wartime hospital cut into the karst above the town road.
hoa-cuong-cave: Hoa Cuong Cave is a rugged, unpolished karst cavern on Cat Ba Island known for its natural crystalline calcite formations and raw underground atmosphere. Unlike more commercialized tourist caves, it offers an authentic, unpaved look at the region's ancient limestone geology.
thien-long-cave-cat-ba: Hang Thiên Long is a local karst cave on Cát Bà Island used on private guide loops and park itineraries. Lighting and access shift here, so confirm the pin before you hire a xe ôm.
nguon-giong-cave: Nguồn Giống Cave is a quiet, natural karst formation located within the buffer zone of Cat Ba National Park. It offers a raw, unlit subterranean experience for visitors seeking to explore the island's geology away from the main tourist circuits.
cannon-fort-cat-ba: Climb Cao Diem 177 above Cat Ba town to inspect French and Vietnamese gun positions, tunnels, and a wide sweep over the harbour and Lan Ha Bay. Access is subject to military restrictions, so verify local status before making the trip up the hill.
cat-co-1: Cát Cò 1 Beach in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Walk or taxi to Bãi Cát Cò 1: the first of the three cliff-backed coves south of town. Development and access paths change; follow signs and swim only where flags allow. The closest cove beach under the town cliffs — sand, deck, weekend noise.
cat-co-2: Cát Cò 2 Beach in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Use Bãi Cát Cò 2 when 1 is packed or a hotel path dumps you here. Same water, same seasonality, same “one beach afternoon” rule. The middle Cát Cò cove — same cliffs, a slightly different deck.
cat-co-3: Cát Cò 3 Beach in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Reach Bãi Cát Cò 3 along the cliff walk or a longer drop from town. Often the least built-up of the three when access is allowed. The farthest Cát Cò cove — quieter sand if the path is open.
tung-thu-beach: Tùng Thu Beach in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Use Bãi Tùng Thu on the harbour edge of Cát Bà town: cafés, evening light, a practical dip when you will not taxi to Cát Cò. The in-town strip — sunset walk more than a swim brochure.
cat-dua-island: Usually on a Lan Hạ day boat, not a separate ticket you must buy. Same water as lan-ha-bay — do not stack a second boat.
viet-hai-village: Boat + transfer; often a half or full day. The viet-hai-fishing-village card is the same commune — do not book twice.
viet-hai-fishing-village: Việt Hải Fishing Village in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Walk the inhabited side of Việt Hải: small boats, gardens, and meals. It is not a second village from the ancient-village card. The working edge of the same Việt Hải valley — nets, gardens, homestay kitchens.
cua-van-via-cat-ba: Cửa Vạn is a historic floating village nestled within the limestone karsts of Ha Long Bay. It serves as a preserved maritime monument reflecting the traditional lifestyle of families who once lived entirely on the water.
cai-beo-village: Explore Cat Ba's ancient floating fishing community at the mouth of the town harbour, still a working aquaculture site. Visit by boat or kayak to experience the historic settlement without booking a full cruise.
hoi-lake: Ho Hoi is a tranquil freshwater lake tucked into the national park hills of Cat Ba Island. It offers a quiet green pause along the main road rather than a bustling swimming resort.
kim-giao-forest: The rare kim giao stand inside Cat Ba National Park offers a shaded botanical walk among endemic trees and jagged limestone karst. It serves as the mandatory first leg of the strenuous climb toward Ngu Lam Peak rather than a standalone viewpoint plaza.
nho-khoi-mountain: Nho Khoi Mountain offers a challenging, rugged trek through the heart of Cat Ba National Park's limestone karst landscape. This is a serious wilderness hike that requires a local guide and physical stamina, far removed from the paved paths of more popular summits.
ngu-lam-peak: Climb Đỉnh Ngự Lâm from the national park entrance via a steep trail of roots and limestone to reach a panoramic viewpoint deck. This standard first hike offers sweeping views of the island's unique karst landscape.
cat-ba-market: Walk Cho Cat Ba in town for wet counters in the morning and quieter lanes by lunch. It is the working day market rather than the evening tourist strip.
cat-ba-night-market: Graze the Cát Bà night market along the harbour streets: grilled shellfish, beer, T-shirts. Agree prices; ice and origin vary.
cat-ba-square: Cát Bà Central Square serves as the main harbour plaza, functioning as the town's primary orientation point for buses, local life, and travel supplies. It provides zero-ticket access for visitors before heading out to rural areas or coastal paths.
cat-ba-cable-car: Cát Bà Cable Car (Sun World Cát Bà) in Cat Ba, Quang Ninh. Ride the Sun World Cát Bà cable car between the Cát Hải mainland station and Phù Long on the island: a long marine karst crossing used as transport and a ticketed viewpoint. It is not the Hạ Long Queen Cable / Sun Wheel. Sun World’s Cát Hải–Phù Long span — a crossing and a view, not a town toy.
phu-long-mangrove: Kayak hire or a short tour; free to look from the road. Same north end as the Sun World cable — one visit.
dong-van-old-quarter: Walk Pho co Dong Van from your stay to experience late-Nguyen and French-period shop houses, a compact central square, and local cafes. The restored area offers a pleasant evening atmosphere on the rocky plateau rather than an untouched historic trading post.
dong-van-old-market: Dong Van Old Market is the everyday covered hall in Ha Giang used for breakfast, produce, and household stalls rather than the Sunday livestock crush. Visitors on ordinary mornings can experience the working rhythm of the old quarter.
vuong-palace-dong-van: Explore the early-20th-century stone and timber courtyards of the Vương family residence at Sà Phìn. This historical mansion offers a rare architectural look into the plateau's opium-era history.
ma-pi-leng-dong-van: Same pass as ma-pi-leng-pass on the Hà Giang page — do not book both. Tu Sản and Nho Que are the same gorge morning.
tu-san-dong-van: Tu San Canyon is the deepest gorge in Southeast Asia, carved by the emerald waters of the Nho Que River beneath the dramatic cliffs of the Ma Pi Leng Pass. Visitors can view this geological wonder either from high roadside lookouts along the pass or by taking a boat ride directly on the river below.
nho-que-dong-van: The Nho Que River winds through a dramatic karst canyon in Ha Giang, featuring a distinct turquoise ribbon of water trapped below the Tu San Gorge. Visitors must descend via a steep mountain road before embarking on motorized boat tours beneath sheer rock walls.
lung-cu-dong-van: The Lung Cu Flag Tower stands as a monumental symbol of sovereignty atop a rugged limestone ridge near the northern border. This site offers a profound look at both national history and the resilient daily life of the ethnic minority communities living within the Dong Van Karst Plateau.
cuc-bac-milestone: Photograph the Cực Bắc milestone on the Lũng Cú spur: a border-area marker sold as the country’s north pole. The true northernmost metre is fussed over; the visit is this stone plus the flag, not a geography exam.
lo-lo-chai-dong-van: Lo Lo Chai Village in Dong Van, Ha Giang. Walk Lô Lô Chải on the Lũng Cú road: distinctive dress, stone houses, a turnout that can feel like a costume stop. The Lô Lô hamlet under the flag — dress, courtyards, easy to stage.
lao-sa-dong-van: Lao Sa Village is a traditional Hmong settlement on the Sung La valley floor in Dong Van, Ha Giang. Visitors experience authentic stone-fence architecture, active hemp weaving, and the famous film house from The Story of Pao.
sung-la-dong-van: Drop into Sung La between Yen Minh and Dong Van to see a green floor of corn, seasonal flowers, and historic earthen-walled houses. It offers a classic plateau road pull-over to observe traditional Hmong valley agriculture.
pao-house-dong-van: Visit Nha Pao in Lao Sa, the lived-in Hmong house featured in the 2006 film The Story of Pao. Experience a traditional northern highland courtyard dwelling instead of a grand palace.
tham-ma-dong-van: Tham Ma Pass is a famous winding mountain pass on the route from Yen Minh to Dong Van in Ha Giang. It offers a striking viewpoint of the serpentine road cutting through the limestone karsts.
chin-khoanh-dong-van: Navigate the dramatic nine-tier hairpin turns of Chin Khoanh Pass along National Highway 4C in Ha Giang. Experience the raw engineering marvel carved directly into the vertical limestone cliffs of the Dong Van Karst Plateau.
ma-le-dong-van: Mã Lé Ancient Village offers older stone Hmong houses on the Lũng Cú spur with a much thinner tourist turnout than neighboring Lô Lô Chải. Walk through quiet stone walls and residential yards along the northern road leading to the flag tower.
sunday-market-dong-van: The Dong Van Sunday Market is a vibrant weekly gathering where highland minority communities converge to trade livestock, textiles, and agricultural goods. It operates exclusively on Sunday mornings as a vital commercial and social hub for the limestone plateau.
ma-le-market: Hit Mã Lé’s weekly market when your host names the morning: a smaller highland trade than Đồng Văn Sunday. Only visit if you are already on that spur and it is market day.
don-cao-fortress: Climb up to the crumbling French-era military post perched above Dong Van for a commanding perspective over the valley and surrounding karst landscape. The steep, winding trail rewards visitors with unmatched geographic context of the northern plateau.
thien-huong-village: Thien Huong is a historic Tay village on the Dong Van plateau, known for its traditional rammed-earth homes. Following severe geological instability in 2024, the original village lanes were closed for safety, and residents were relocated to a nearby resettlement area.
lung-ngoc-ho-cave: Hang Lung Ngoc Ho is a rugged, uncommercialized karst cave in the Dong Van plateau that requires local arrangement and careful footing. It offers an exploratory caving experience for travelers who prefer raw geology over paved tourist walkways.
pho-cao-village: Pho Cao Village sits in the rocky plateau of Dong Van district, featuring dense clusters of earthen-walled houses set against dry corn terraces. It offers an alternative Hmong settlement experience for travelers seeking quieter loops away from busier tourist hubs.
pho-bang-ancient-town: Pho Bang is a remote highland trading settlement nestled in a deep limestone valley of Ha Giang Province. It features dense clusters of traditional rammed-earth houses and weathered timber doors that reflect a slower, unpolished pace of daily life.
lung-cam-village: Lung Cam Cultural Village is a traditional community-tourism settlement in Dong Van, Ha Giang, featuring historic stone-walled Hmong homes. Visitors can explore authentic earth-walled architecture, stone courtyards, and local agricultural life without the heavy crowds of major Sunday markets.
xuan-huong-lake: Loop Xuan Huong Lake on foot or by bike through Da Lat’s cool highland center — gardens, cafés, and swan boats. A gentle first afternoon that sets the pace for Crazy House or Valley of Love.
crazy-house: Explore Hang Nga’s whimsical concrete sculptures, tunnels, and viewpoint rooms. This surreal treehouse architecture in Da Lat is designed for visitors to climb through like a living dream.
valley-of-love: Explore the terraced hills, pine forests, and manicured flower gardens of Da Lat's most famous landscaped parkland. Rent a swan pedal boat on Da Da Thien Lake and walk the winding paths overlooking the valley.
datanla-waterfall: Ride or walk down to Datanla’s falls in the pines south of town. Active Da Lat without needing a full canyoning day.
da-lat-night-market: Wander Hoa Binh night market for snacks, souvenirs, and cool-air crowds. Experience the highland evening that is actually the plan.
tuyen-lam-lake: Large reservoir south of the centre. Shore paths and boats are free-to-cheap; the Robin Hill cable car (~100,000đ return) drops you at Trúc Lâm above the water.
lake-of-sighs: Visit Hồ Than Thở, a quieter lake east of the centre named for a tragic folk story, with pine paths and a small island shrine. Experience atmosphere without Xuan Huong’s traffic.
da-lat-railway-station: Heritage station (1932–38) with three triangular roofs. Grounds and hall from about 07:00; a viewing fee may apply.
da-lat-cathedral: St. Nicholas Cathedral in Da Lat is an iconic 20th-century Romanesque landmark crowned by a distinctive bronze rooster weathervane. Visitors can examine its Grenoble stained glass and sturdy brick architecture while navigating limited interior access around service times.
domaine-de-marie: Walk the Domaine de Marie compound: 1940s pink church, gardens, and the convent that still sells handmade knitwear. Quieter and prettier than the Chicken Church for most photographs.
linh-phuoc-pagoda: Linh Phuoc Pagoda in Trai Mat is a flamboyant Vietnamese temple complex famous for its monumental dragon constructed from a million discarded glass bottles. Visitors come to inspect the intricate ceramic mosaic work, the towering bell structure, and the underground chambers.
truc-lam-monastery: Trúc Lâm Zen Monastery is an active Buddhist center perched on the slopes of Phụng Hoàng Mountain overlooking Tuyền Lâm Lake. It offers a serene environment for meditation, featuring minimalist architecture, manicured gardens, and expansive views of the Da Lat highlands.
linh-an-pagoda: Stop at Linh An for the large outdoor Buddha, halls, and a quieter courtyard than Linh Phuoc's mosaics. Experience a calm pagoda on the way to Prenn or Tuyen Lam.
thien-vuong-pagoda: Visit Thien Vuong Co Sat, a Taiwanese-built monastery known locally as Chua Tau, for its three huge Buddha statues and pine setting. Experience scale without Linh Phuoc's bottle kitsch while walking through this hillside monastic complex in Da Lat.
bao-dai-palace-i: Bảo Đại Summer Palace I sits high on a quiet pine ridge in Da Lat as a ticketed heritage house with sweeping valley views. This hilltop estate offers a distinct historical glimpse into the former emperor's life, separate from the more heavily visited Dinh III.
bao-dai-palace-ii: Palace II on Trần Hưng Đạo (1933–37). Hours listed 07:00–17:30 and about 50,000đ when public; it is frequently closed as an official guesthouse.
bao-dai-palace-iii: Bảo Đại Summer Palace III in Da Lat. Tour Dinh III on Triệu Việt Vương, Bảo Đại’s main Da Lat home (1933–38), preserved as a house museum. The palace everyone means — Art Deco interiors in Ái Ân pine forest.
lam-vien-square: Lâm Viên Square in Da Lat. Lam Vien Square (Vietnamese: Quảng trường Lâm Viên) is the central square of the former city of Da Lat, Lâm Đồng Province. It has become one of Da Lat's most popular public spaces and a major venue for cultural and tourism events, including Dalat Flower Festival. Name In its early days, the square was named Đà Lạt Central Square (Quảng trường Trung tâm Đà Lạt) and it still used as an colloquial name. Artichoke towers and evening lights on Xuân Hương’s edge.
clay-tunnel-dalat: Walk the open-air sculpture trench near Tuyền Lâm: red-clay figures of Da Lat history, the Faces of Love, and a lakeside café at the end. It is weird in a different way from Crazy House and it is not an underground tunnel.
elephant-falls: Descend to Thác Voi in Nam Ban, a powerful cascade often combined with Pongour on a southern loop. If Datanla felt like a theme park, this is the corrective.
pongour-waterfall: Pongour Waterfall is a wide, multi-tiered natural cascade located south of Da Lat in Lam Dong Province. It is best known for its dramatic horizontal basalt steps rather than a single vertical drop.
prenn-waterfall: Prenn Waterfall is a landscaped cascade situated just south of Da Lat along the main pass road. Visitors can walk directly behind the curtain of falling water without taking a long journey out of town.
tiger-cave-waterfall: Walk Tiger Cave Waterfall for a compact cave-and-cascade stop, cheaper and quieter than Datanla’s coaster park. A small wild fall if the big names are booked with tour buses.
cam-ly-waterfall: Cam Ly Waterfall is the closest cascade to the center of Da Lat, set within a manicured park with a modest entry fee. It offers a convenient in-town water view, though visitors often compare it unfavorably to the larger falls outside the city.
dambri-waterfall: Dambri Waterfall is a powerful, high-altitude cascade located in the lush tea-growing region of Bao Loc. It offers a full-day experience featuring a glass elevator, forest trails, and an alpine coaster set within a dense, humid rainforest environment.
langbiang: Climb or jeep Langbiang for plateau views, pine ridgelines, and the mountain that names the highlands in local memory. Experience the altitude and wind after too many flower parks on this iconic peak above Lat village.
da-lat-flower-gardens: The municipal flower park on Xuan Huong's north shore featuring seasonal beds, greenhouses, and a short lakeside garden that is not a working village. Walk through terraced horticultural displays and topiary arrangements without driving to the outer agricultural valleys.
van-thanh-flowers: Vạn Thành Flower Village in Da Lat. Wander Vạn Thành’s flower lanes and plastic-house rows, the production village behind Da Lat’s market bunches. Working greenhouses on the west side — roses you can smell.
thai-phien-flowers: Ride out to Thai Phien for broader flower fields and family farms, a counterpart to Van Thanh's tighter lanes. Experience working agriculture with space and fewer photo-stall operators.
cau-dat-tea: Visit Cầu Đất’s historic tea plantation for contour rows, a hill café, and the coolest air on a clear day. This highland landscape provides a vast expanse that is neither crowded flower gardens nor typical cascading waterfalls.
da-lat-market: Shop Cho Da Lat in daylight for fresh produce, preserved fruit jams, and warm layers. This working agricultural hall feeds the city before the night market begins.
fairytale-land-dalat: Walk Fairytale Land’s miniature village, seasonal flowers, and optional wine cellar on the west-side photo-farm strip. A short, staged park — fine with kids, skippable if you dislike props.
lumiere-light-garden: Walk Lumiere’s illuminated garden paths and installations after sunset, a ticketed evening attraction. This is a night garden, not a farm, offering after-dark flower lights for when the night market is enough food and you still want a walk.
hydrangea-trai-mat: Explore the sprawling terraced hydrangea fields of Trai Mat, a working agricultural valley near Da Lat accessible via the heritage railway. Photograph dense clusters of blue and purple blossoms while respecting local farming plots.
fresh-garden-dalat: Fresh Garden Dalat is a designed flower park located on the Van Thanh strip, offering landscaped beds and constructed photo installations. It provides a more manicured landscape than working vegetable greenhouses while remaining distinct from adjacent themed attractions.
cu-lan-village: Cu Lan Village is a privately developed resort and staged highland-themed park nestled in a pine-shaded valley north of Da Lat. Visitors can explore wooden stilt houses, artificial streams, and recreational activity zones alongside a simulated ethnic minority aesthetic.
chicken-village-kho: Stop in Đồng K’Ho for a traditional K’Ho ethnic minority settlement, local weaving stalls, and the oversized concrete chicken sculpture that gave the village its famous roadside moniker. Walk the paths respectfully to observe daily highland life at the foot of Langbiang Mountain.
mongo-land-dalat: Mongo Land Dalat is a colourful roadside adventure park on the Tà Nung pass featuring a rainbow slide, animal enclosures, and valley views. It makes a lively, active family stop between longer waterfall excursions.
french-quarter-dalat: Walk the hill-station villa quarter along Tran Hung Dao and surrounding streets to see colonial French houses, steep pine lanes, and the architectural fabric that defines Da Lat. This is a free open-air experience of the city's historic core.
hundred-roofs-bar: Navigate 100 Roofs (Ngan Mai): a multi-level maze bar of tiny tiled roofs, corners, and a cocktail at the end. Enjoy nightlife that is actually a sight, not a beer street.
thousand-year-banyan: A massive heritage banyan with roots like natural columns, a quiet stop on the northern peninsula loop. Do not leave the path or feed wildlife nearby.
phu-tay-ho: Visit the spiritual complex dedicated to Liễu Hạnh on a peninsula jutting into Hồ Tây. Locals come for prayers at full moons and Tết; food stalls outside serve crispy shrimp cakes.
turtle-lake-saigon: Turtle Lake is a 1960s modernist roundabout and evening hangout in District 3, ringed by busy street food stalls. Visit after dark to experience the vibrant local youth culture and lively social energy.
trang-tien-plaza: Trang Tien Plaza is a grand colonial-era department store building located at the southeastern corner of Hoan Kiem Lake. It blends historic French architecture with high-end modern retail, offering a polished, air-conditioned respite in central Hanoi.
gia-dinh-park: Gia Định Park is a sprawling eucalyptus and banyan canopy in Phú Nhuận District used daily for morning jogging, aerobics, and neighborhood gatherings. It offers visitors a genuine look at Saigon's local fitness culture away from standard tourist monuments.
hanoi-weekend-night-market: The Hanoi Weekend Night Market fills Hang Dao street with handicrafts, street food, apparel, and live music from Friday through Sunday evening. It is the easiest evening circuit for shopping and people-watching in the historic core.
factory-contemporary-arts: The Factory Contemporary Arts Centre is Thảo Điền’s landmark space for rotating contemporary Vietnamese and Southeast Asian art installations. Housed in a striking industrial structure made of stacked shipping containers, it serves as an active hub for experimental art, public education, and creative exchange.
phan-xich-long: Phan Xich Long is Phu Nhuan district's primary culinary boulevard, packed with restaurants, milk tea shops, and street stalls. It offers an authentic neighborhood dining experience with local prices rather than a sanitized tourist food court circuit.
ban-co-peak: Ban Co Peak is the highest accessible point on the Son Tra Peninsula, featuring a bronze statue of an immortal playing chess alongside panoramic views. Visitors must navigate steep, winding mountain roads to reach the summit for sweeping coastal vistas.
